```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(here)
library(lavaan)
step_dir <- here("phase2-1-scale-development", "03_cfa-structures")
out_dir  <- file.path(step_dir, "output")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## What this notebook does

Step 01 extracts EFA solutions with 1 to 6 factors and reports their fit (`psych::fa`). In an EFA every item loads on
every factor, so the fit describes the free solution. This notebook tests the same structures as **confirmatory**
models: each item loads only on the factor of its largest EFA loading, all other loadings are fixed at zero, and the
factors are allowed to correlate. The fit of these models can then be compared with the EFA fit and judged with the
usual CFA criteria (Hu & Bentler, 1999).

- **Data:** whole sample (506), 65 items, rare options collapsed (as in the EFA). Single group: the tools are pooled.
- **Structures:** from `01_efa/output/loadings/pa-<k>-factors-agg.csv` (k = 1–6). For k = 3 the assignment is the
  `full_UX_3_factors` list of the paper (25, 18 and 22 items).
- **Estimators:**
  - `ML` with full-information maximum likelihood for missing answers (`missing = "fiml"`), as in the manual CFA
    testing of phase 2.2;
  - `WLSMV` with the items declared ordinal (`ordered = TRUE`, pairwise handling of missing answers), which uses
    polychoric correlations like the EFA. Its fit indices are the scaled ones.
- Factors are identified by fixing their variances to 1 (`std.lv = TRUE`).

## Data and structures

```{r data}
d <- read.csv(here(params$data_file), check.names = FALSE)
d <- d[, setdiff(names(d), c("seed", "stimulus"))]
items <- names(d)

read_loadings <- function(k) {
  r <- read.csv(file.path(here(params$efa_dir), "loadings", sprintf("pa-%d-factors-agg.csv", k)), check.names = FALSE)
  r <- r[seq_len(which(r$terms == "--- VARIANCE EXPLAINED ---") - 1), ]
  L <- as.matrix(r[, -1, drop = FALSE]); rownames(L) <- r$terms
  storage.mode(L) <- "numeric"
  L[items, , drop = FALSE]
}

structures <- lapply(seq_len(params$n_factors_max), function(k) {
  L <- read_loadings(k)
  setNames(colnames(L)[apply(L, 1, which.max)], items)   # factor of the largest loading
})

assignment <- data.frame(item = items, sapply(structures, identity))
names(assignment)[-1] <- paste0("factor_in_", seq_len(params$n_factors_max), "_factor_model")
write.csv(assignment, file.path(out_dir, "item-assignment.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

model_syntax <- function(s) {
  paste(sapply(sort(unique(s)), function(f) paste0(f, " =~ ", paste(names(s)[s == f], collapse = " + "))),
        collapse = "\n")
}
data.frame(factors = seq_len(params$n_factors_max),
           items_per_factor = sapply(structures, function(s) paste(table(factor(s, levels = sort(unique(s)))), collapse = ", ")))
```

## CFA of each structure

With FIML, `lavaan::fitMeasures` takes about 100 s per model for each of RMSEA and CFI. The ML indices are therefore
computed here from the χ² of the model and of the independence model (fitted once, it is the same for every
structure), with the formulas `lavaan` uses. For the 1-factor model they were checked against `fitMeasures`
(CFI 0.800, TLI 0.794, RMSEA 0.057 [0.056, 0.059]): identical.

```{r fit-indices-ml}
baseline <- NULL
fit_indices_ml <- function(fit) {
  if (is.null(baseline)) baseline <<- lavaan:::lav_object_independence(fit)
  x2 <- unname(fitMeasures(fit, "chisq")); df <- unname(fitMeasures(fit, "df")); N <- lavInspect(fit, "ntotal")
  x2b <- unname(fitMeasures(baseline, "chisq")); dfb <- unname(fitMeasures(baseline, "df"))
  rmsea_ci <- function(p) {
    f0 <- function(l) pchisq(x2, df, ncp = l) - p
    if (f0(0) < 0) return(0)
    sqrt(uniroot(f0, c(0, max(10 * x2, 1)))$root / (df * N))
  }
  c(chisq = x2, df = df,
    cfi = 1 - max(x2 - df, 0) / max(x2 - df, x2b - dfb, 0),
    tli = ((x2b / dfb) - (x2 / df)) / ((x2b / dfb) - 1),
    rmsea = sqrt(max((x2 - df) / (df * N), 0)), rmsea_lower = rmsea_ci(0.95), rmsea_upper = rmsea_ci(0.05),
    srmr = unname(fitMeasures(fit, "srmr")), bic = unname(fitMeasures(fit, "bic")))
}
```

```{r cfa}
fit_one <- function(k, estimator) {
  model <- model_syntax(structures[[k]])
  fit <- if (estimator == "ML") {
    # Starting values from the listwise solution: with lavaan's default start the FIML fit of the 5-factor
    # structure did not finish in 15 minutes; with these it converges in about 50 iterations. The estimates are
    # the FIML ones either way.
    start <- cfa(model, data = d, estimator = "ML", std.lv = TRUE)
    cfa(model, data = d, estimator = "ML", missing = "fiml", std.lv = TRUE, start = start)
  } else {
    cfa(model, data = d, ordered = items, estimator = "WLSMV", missing = "pairwise", std.lv = TRUE)
  }
  idx <- if (estimator == "ML") {
    fit_indices_ml(fit)
  } else {
    m <- fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq.scaled", "df.scaled", "cfi.scaled", "tli.scaled", "rmsea.scaled",
                            "rmsea.ci.lower.scaled", "rmsea.ci.upper.scaled", "srmr"))
    c(m, bic = NA)
  }
  names(idx) <- c("chisq", "df", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "rmsea_lower", "rmsea_upper", "srmr", "bic")
  data.frame(factors = k, estimator = estimator, n = lavInspect(fit, "nobs"),
             converged = lavInspect(fit, "converged"), t(idx), row.names = NULL)
}

cfa_fit <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("ML", "WLSMV"), function(e)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(params$n_factors_max), fit_one, estimator = e))))
write.csv(cfa_fit, file.path(out_dir, "cfa-fit-by-structure.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(cfa_fit, digits = 3)
```

The **Hu and Bentler** combinations: SRMR ≤ .08 with CFI or TLI ≥ .95, or SRMR ≤ .08 with RMSEA ≤ .06.

Correlations between the factors (WLSMV), to see whether the extra factors of the 4–6 factor structures are distinct:

```{r factor-correlations}
lv_cor <- do.call(rbind, lapply(2:params$n_factors_max, function(k) {
  fit <- cfa(model_syntax(structures[[k]]), data = d, ordered = items, estimator = "WLSMV",
             missing = "pairwise", std.lv = TRUE)
  r <- lavInspect(fit, "cor.lv")
  u <- r[upper.tri(r)]
  data.frame(factors = k, min_factor_correlation = min(u), max_factor_correlation = max(u))
}))
write.csv(lv_cor, file.path(out_dir, "factor-correlations-wlsmv.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(lv_cor, digits = 2)
```

```{r hu-bentler}
cfa_fit$hu_bentler <- with(cfa_fit, srmr <= .08 & (cfi >= .95 | tli >= .95 | rmsea <= .06))
knitr::kable(cfa_fit[, c("factors", "estimator", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr", "hu_bentler")], digits = 3)
```

## EFA fit and CFA fit side by side

```{r efa-vs-cfa}
efa_fit <- read.csv(file.path(here(params$efa_dir), "fit-indices.csv"))
efa_fit <- efa_fit[efa_fit$group == "Agg", ]
wide <- function(e) {
  x <- cfa_fit[cfa_fit$estimator == e, c("factors", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr", "bic")]
  names(x)[-1] <- paste0("cfa_", tolower(e), "_", names(x)[-1]); x
}
side <- merge(data.frame(factors = efa_fit$factors, efa_cfi = efa_fit$cfi, efa_tli = efa_fit$tli, efa_rmsea = efa_fit$rmsea,
                         efa_rmsr = efa_fit$rmsr, efa_bic = efa_fit$bic),
              merge(wide("ML"), wide("WLSMV")[, c("factors", "cfa_wlsmv_cfi", "cfa_wlsmv_tli", "cfa_wlsmv_rmsea",
                                                  "cfa_wlsmv_srmr")], by = "factors"), by = "factors")
write.csv(side, file.path(out_dir, "efa-vs-cfa-fit.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(side, digits = 3)
```

LaTeX table of the CFA fit for the paper (`output/table-cfa-fit.tex`, needs `booktabs`):

```{r cfa-table-tex}
num <- function(x, d) sub("^-", "$-$", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","))
ml <- cfa_fit[cfa_fit$estimator == "ML", ]
wl <- cfa_fit[cfa_fit$estimator == "WLSMV", ]
rows <- sprintf("%d & %s & %s & %s [%s, %s] & %s & %s & & %s & %s & %s & %s \\\\",
                ml$factors, num(ml$cfi, 3), num(ml$tli, 3), num(ml$rmsea, 3), num(ml$rmsea_lower, 3),
                num(ml$rmsea_upper, 3), num(ml$srmr, 3), num(ml$bic, 0),
                num(wl$cfi, 3), num(wl$tli, 3), num(wl$rmsea, 3), num(wl$srmr, 3))
writeLines(c(
  "\\begin{table}[htbp]",
  "\\centering",
  "\\caption{Fit of confirmatory factor models of the 1 to 6 factor structures (whole sample, $N = 506$; each item loads only on the factor of its largest EFA loading). ML: maximum likelihood with FIML; WLSMV: items treated as ordinal (scaled indices).}",
  "\\label{tab:cfa-fit}",
  "\\begin{tabular}{rrrcrrcrrrr}",
  "\\toprule",
  " & \\multicolumn{5}{c}{ML (FIML)} & & \\multicolumn{4}{c}{WLSMV} \\\\",
  "\\cmidrule(lr){2-6} \\cmidrule(lr){8-11}",
  "Factors & CFI & TLI & RMSEA [90\\% CI] & SRMR & BIC & & CFI & TLI & RMSEA & SRMR \\\\",
  "\\midrule",
  rows,
  "\\bottomrule",
  "\\end{tabular}",
  "\\end{table}"), file.path(out_dir, "table-cfa-fit.tex"))
cat(readLines(file.path(out_dir, "table-cfa-fit.tex")), sep = "\n")
```

Reading the table:

- The EFA indices come from `psych::fa` (principal axis on the polychoric matrix). `psych` computes χ², TLI, RMSEA
  and BIC with a maximum-likelihood formula and reports RMSR, the root mean square of the residual correlations,
  which is close to but not the same as the SRMR of a CFA.
- The CFA indices come from `lavaan`. The CFA is more restrictive (no cross-loadings), but its indices are computed
  on a different basis (raw data with ML, or the ordinal model with WLSMV), so the two sets are not directly
  comparable: a CFA index can be higher than the EFA one.
- BIC is comparable only within one column. For the EFA and for the ML CFA, lower is better.
